=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Bottom line:** The Seller calls this package "fair and balanced". It is not. Three positions work together to remove the protection our warranties are supposed to give:

- **General disclosure** of the whole data room and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Constructive buyer knowledge** (cl 8.3)
- **Limitations applying to "all Claims"** (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)

As drafted, almost every issue we already know about would be unrecoverable. Several of those issues also go unresolved at Completion: the Bluefen consent, the Riverlark debt, the AUD 420k bonuses, Ironquay IP and the DD-006 incident. Some of the Seller's own covering statements are contradicted by its Disclosure Letter, and we should point that out in our response.

*Caveat:* this review is based only on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. Clause references and the points below should be checked against them.

---

## A. Structural issues (fix these first)

### 1. Disclosure regime (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Problem:** Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records means any item buried anywhere qualifies every warranty.
- **Push back:**
  - Only **specific disclosures** in the Disclosure Letter should qualify the warranties.
  - Each must be **fairly disclosed**, meaning in enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
  - Delete the public-records disclosure. At most, allow searches of named registers on a stated date.
  - If data-room disclosure is conceded at all, limit it to a fixed, indexed, archived copy (USB) and keep the "fairly disclosed" standard.
  - No updating of disclosure between signing and Completion against repeated warranties. If updates are allowed, a material new matter should give us a termination right.

### 2. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Problem:** The clause covers knowledge of "the Buyer *or its advisers*" and anything "*discoverable*" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge, and it lets the Seller defeat claims on exactly the matters our due diligence uncovered.
- **Push back:**
  - Our preferred position is that the Buyer's knowledge does not affect any claim (pro-sandbagging).
  - As a fallback, limit it to **actual knowledge** of named deal-team individuals, excluding advisers, and expressly exclude **specific indemnities, tax, title and fraud**.

### 3. "Limitations apply to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Problem:** The cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions would extend to fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, tax, leakage and price-adjustment claims, and even fraud.
- **Push back:** Reverse the default. Limitations apply **only to general Warranty Claims** unless the SPA expressly says otherwise. Carve out entirely:
  - **fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment**, by the Seller or its officers or advisers;
  - specific indemnities;
  - title and capacity;
  - tax;
  - leakage, price adjustment and completion payment obligations.
- **Non-reliance:** It cannot exclude liability for fraud. Under Australian Consumer Law s 18 we should still resist a broad non-reliance clause and keep reliance on the warranties and the Disclosure Letter.

### 4. Fundamental warranties subject to the general cap and time limits
- **Problem:** The Seller wants title and capacity limited to AUD 4.8m and 18 months "for administrative simplicity". This is unacceptable. If title fails, we lose the whole AUD 24m.
- **Push back:**
  - **Cap:** 100% of the purchase price.
  - **Time limit:** at least 6–7 years (compare the NSW contract limitation period).
  - **Thresholds:** de minimis and basket do not apply.

### 5. Caps, thresholds and time limits for general warranties (cl 12.1–12.3)

| Item | Seller | Comment | Buyer ask |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Within market range only if fundamentals, tax and indemnities sit outside it | 30–50%. Concede 20% only as a trade for the carve-outs above |
| De minimis | AUD 25k per claim | ~0.1% of price, high-ish | AUD 10–15k; related claims aggregated |
| Basket | AUD 250k, deductible (excess only) | ~1.04%, and deductible favours the Seller | **Tipping** basket at ~0.5% (AUD 120k), recovering from the first dollar |
| Time limit | 18 months | Acceptable for general warranties | 18–24 months, covering at least one full audit cycle |
| Tax | "Settled under general regime" | Not acceptable | Standalone tax indemnity, 100% cap, ~5–7 years (beyond ATO amendment periods) |

- **Security for claims:** Ask whether W&I insurance is planned. If not, seek a **retention or escrow**, for example 10% (AUD 2.4m) for 18–24 months, plus specific retentions for the issues below.

---

## B. Deal-specific issues

### 6. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): **Critical**
- **The risk:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and its contract contains a change-control clause (cl 11.2).
- **The contradiction:** The Seller says the consent is "addressed", but its own disclosure (item 2) says there is **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.
- **Why "satisfied on delivery of written consent" is not enough:** Consent alone does not show the 11.3 conditions are met, and the consent could be conditional or carry adverse terms.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **condition precedent** that only the Buyer can waive.
  - The consent must be unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied and the consent not withdrawn at Completion.
  - Upgrade the Seller's obligation to **all reasonable** or best endeavours, with Buyer participation in approaches to Bluefen.
  - The Seller bears any cost of satisfying the conditions.
  - Include a long-stop date and a Buyer walk right.
  - Consider a price adjustment or earn-out protection if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within, say, 12 months.

### 7. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): **Critical**
- **Why the Seller's position fails:** A "release to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with a **debt-free/cash-free** deal.
  - The facility (~AUD 3.2m) has a change-control clause (8.1), so Completion is likely to trigger an event of default.
  - Disclosure item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in hand.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat it as **Debt**, deducted from the price and repaid directly from Completion funds.
  - At Completion, require:
    - a payout letter;
    - an executed deed of release;
    - PPSR financing-change/discharge statements;
    - releases of any guarantees or security, **including any security over the Sale Shares**.
  - Add a Seller indemnity for any residual amount.

### 8. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k): **High**
- **Why it matters:** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" yet leaves them out of the funds flow. The Company is the employer, so it will bear the liability, and the payments are triggered by Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses as **Transaction Costs / Debt-like items**, deducted from the price.
  - Include all **on-costs**: payroll tax, any superannuation, workers' comp and PAYG withholding. The Disclosure Letter is silent on these.
  - Pay through payroll at Completion or into a trust/escrow account.
  - Add a Seller indemnity.
  - Clarify the continued-employment conditions. Any post-Completion retention element should be funded by the Seller. The Buyer should not end up paying it.

### 9. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1): **High**
- **The risk:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until **every SOW3 fee** has cleared. AUD 180k is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment (item 4). The Company may therefore not own IP in its product.
- **Why the existing indemnity falls short:** It only covers the payment. The real exposure is ownership and infringement, including injunction risk, re-engineering cost and customer claims.
- **Push back:**
  - **Before Completion**, require evidence of cleared payment plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** (and moral rights consents) from Ironquay, as a CP or Completion deliverable.
  - Extend the indemnity to all Loss from any failure of title to, or third-party claim over, SOW3 materials.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the cap, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge limitations, supported by a retention.

### 10. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6): **High, time-sensitive**
- **The contradiction:** The Seller says the incident is "not expected to be material". Its own disclosure (item 6) says access, scope and notification are all **unknown** and the investigation is preliminary. About 1,240 records of personal information are involved.
- **The timing issue:** Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC), an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment, generally **within 30 days**. The incident was already known by 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November. There is a real risk the assessment or notification obligations have already been missed. This should be confirmed urgently.
- **Push back:**
  - **Before signing:** obtain the forensic or investigation report, link-access logs, the NDB assessment and the notification decision, and any OAIC or customer correspondence.
  - **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident (regulatory, remediation, notification, customer and third-party claims). It should sit outside the general limitations and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge, supported by a retention.
  - Add a pre-Completion covenant to conduct the response properly, with Buyer consultation.
  - Consider a CP or walk right if the incident proves to be a notifiable breach with material exposure.

### 11. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k): **Medium**
- **The concern:** The Seller calls these "ordinary course", but the Disclosure Letter (item 8) does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
  - Three *related* renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Disclosure Letter itself says should be read together, may have been structured to stay under an approval threshold. This is speculation for now and needs checking against the conduct-of-business covenant.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain the contracts and check timing against signing and any locked-box date.
  - If they are not genuinely ordinary course or needed Buyer consent, treat them as leakage or a debt-like item, or require termination at Seller cost.
  - Add a warranty on terminability and on no prepayments.

### 12. Title (DD-012): **Medium**
- **The gap:** A share register alone is not enough, and item 10 itself says Buyer verification is not confirmed.
- **Push back:**
  - **Verification:** obtain the full register history, share certificates, ASIC company extracts and a PPSR search over the shares and the Company.
  - **Warranty:** no options, convertibles or other rights to shares.
  - **Completion deliverables:** transfer forms, certificates and releases of any encumbrance (cross-check Riverlark).
  - **Limits:** title is a fundamental warranty, uncapped up to the price (see item 4).

### 13. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): **Low to medium**
- **Lease:** Make the landlord notification a Seller covenant or Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale:** Get a specific warranty that no third-party consent is triggered by the share sale under the lease, the Mossvale contract or any other material contract. Do not rely on the Seller's characterisation.

### 14. Tax and IP warranties
- **Not "settled":**
  - **Tax:** a full tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods.
  - **IP:** IP warranties should carry an extended time limit and possibly a higher cap, given that Paperbark is an analytics business whose value lies in its IP and data.

---

## C. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Priority | Our position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General disclosure | Critical | Specific, fair disclosure only; no public-record or deemed disclosure |
| 2 | Buyer knowledge cl 8.3 | Critical | Delete, or limit to actual knowledge of named individuals; exclude indemnities, tax, title, fraud |
| 3 | Limitations apply to all Claims | Critical | General warranties only; carve out fraud, fundamentals, indemnities, tax, leakage |
| 4 | Fundamentals under general cap | Critical | 100% of price, 6–7 years, no thresholds |
| 5 | Bluefen consent | Critical | Buyer-waivable CP; unconditional consent with 11.3 satisfied; stronger endeavours; long-stop and walk right |
| 6 | Riverlark debt | Critical | Repay from price at Completion; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharges as deliverables |
| 7 | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | High | Deduct from price; pay via payroll at Completion; indemnity |
| 8 | Ironquay IP | High | Pre-Completion payment proof and confirmatory assignment; broad uncapped IP indemnity; retention |
| 9 | DD-006 incident | High, urgent | Diligence the NDB position now; specific indemnity outside limits; retention; possible CP |
| 10 | Cap, basket, de minimis | Medium–High | 30–50% cap (20% only as a trade); tipping basket ~AUD 120k; de minimis AUD 10–15k |
| 11 | Tax | High | Standalone tax indemnity, 100% cap, ~5–7 years |
| 12 | Sandbar renewals | Medium | Verify; treat as leakage or debt-like if not ordinary course |
| 13 | Title verification | Medium | Full register history, certificates, ASIC and PPSR searches; encumbrance releases |
| 14 | Security for claims | High | W&I and/or escrow (~10%) plus specific retentions for items 8 and 9 |

**Next steps:**
1. **Today:** send an urgent diligence request on DD-006 (NDB assessment status) and Ironquay (payment evidence).
2. **With our mark-up:** ask for a Bluefen status update and a Riverlark payout figure.
3. **In the mark-up:** reverse the structural positions (A1–A4) before negotiating the numbers.
4. **Funds flow:** revise it to show Riverlark repayment and bonuses plus on-costs as deductions from the AUD 24m price.

  - If they are not genuinely ordinary course or needed Buyer consent, treat them as leakage or a debt-like item, or require termination at Seller cost.
  - Add a warranty on terminability and on no prepayments.

### 12. Title (DD-012): **Medium**
- **The gap:** A share register alone is not enough, and item 10 itself says Buyer verification is not confirmed.
- **Push back:**
  - **Verification:** obtain the full register history, share certificates, ASIC company extracts and a PPSR search over the shares and the Company.
  - **Warranty:** no options, convertibles or other rights to shares.
  - **Completion deliverables:** transfer forms, certificates and releases of any encumbrance (cross-check Riverlark).
  - **Limits:** title is a fundamental warranty, uncapped up to the price (see item 4).

### 13. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): **Low to medium**
- **Lease:** Make the landlord notification a Seller covenant or Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale:** Get a specific warranty that no third-party consent is triggered by the share sale under the lease, the Mossvale contract or any other material contract. Do not rely on the Seller's characterisation.

### 14. Tax and IP warranties
- **Not "settled":**
  - **Tax:** a full tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods.
  - **IP:** IP warranties should carry an extended time limit and possibly a higher cap, given that Paperbark is an analytics business whose value lies in its IP and data.
